rfm_tuples.M_value: OBBBA Section 45X applies to U.S.-produced metallurgical coal beginning in 2026, at 2.5% of production-related costs, sunsetting end-2029. Q1 2026 metallurgical segment cash cost of coal sold per ton = $92.35, on 2.5M tons sold = ~$231M of cash production costs in Q1 alone; annualized ~$924M of qualifying base. A 2.5% credit applied to ~$900M annual production cost base would be ~$22-25M of annual federal tax credits, monetizable. Over the 4-year window (2026-2029), this is ~$90-100M of pre-tax-equivalent value to CNR. The Q1 2026 10-Q does NOT yet accrue any OBBBA benefit (the income tax line is small — only $0.4M benefit on $20.6M pre-tax income — and management says the credit determination depends on Treasury rulings). Management's 'currently evaluating' language is appropriately conservative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-A passes. Mode-B finding is FAVORABLE to CNR: management has not yet booked any OBBBA Section 45X benefit in the Q1 2026 results, but the credit when implemented (likely starting in late 2026 / 2027 after Treasury guidance) would add ~$22-25M of annual benefit through 2029. The Q1 2026 metallurgical segment cash margin of $19.68/ton already reflects a 904% sequential improvement from $1.96/ton in Q4 2025 (driven by lower cost of coal sold per ton and higher Premium Low-Vol pricing); the OBBBA tailwind sits ON TOP of this and is NOT in the Q1 EBITDA print. This is a counter-signal to the broader 'distressed energy small-cap' framing of the forward-test group: there is a real, legislated, pre-cutoff tailwind that is being conservatively reported.

summary: CNR (Core Natural Resources) is a post-merger coal name (CONSOL+Arch combined Jan 14, 2025) whose -25.8% pre-cutoff drawdown is driven by commodity-cycle de-rating and Leer South operational overhang, NOT balance-sheet distress. The disclosure trust picture is mixed-positive: Q1 2026 normalized strongly (net income $21M, adj EBITDA $180M, FCF $55.5M, met-segment cash margin per ton up 904% sequentially); liquidity is $935M with net cash position; auditor (E&Y) is clean and no going-concern flag; OBBBA Section 45X met-coal 2.5% production tax credit (effective 2026-2029) is conservatively NOT yet accrued. The negative findings center on Form-4 Mode-B signals: ZERO open-market Code-P purchases by any officer or director across 299 pre-cutoff Form-4 filings, while the CEO (Brock, 40,760 sh @ $101.15) and CLO (Klein, 15,000 sh @ avg $106.87, the highest insider sale price observed) sold in a clustered Q1-2026 mid-March window at prices ~10% above the company's own buyback average — the inverse of the canonical commitment signal. Additional moderate negatives: ~$72M residual uninsured Leer South loss with slowing recovery pace, and a fresh pre-cutoff May 2026 cluster of two MSHA section 107(a) imminent-danger methane orders (Mountaineer II Apr 29, Leer South May 13 — the Leer South order was vacated as 'imminent danger never existed' on May 18). Severity counts: P=4 / M=3 / S=1 / R=0 / U=0. Verdict: NEUTRAL — the balance-sheet strength, OBBBA tailwind, and Q1 2026 operational rebound largely offset the absent-commitment Form-4 signal and Leer South operational fragility. This is NOT a SHORT-tier candidate (no liquidity distress, no governance scandal, no commitment-narrative break of the CCOI/SRPT magnitude). It is also not a LONG-tier candidate due to the Form-4 commitment-signal failure.
